result.summary: The image depicts an urban intersection with marked zebra crosswalks and sidewalks on both sides of the street. While traffic signals and 'No Turn on Red' signage are present, the environment lacks visible dedicated pedestrian signals and refuge islands for the multi-lane crossing.

hazards.name: Lack of visible pedestrian signals
hazards.description: No dedicated pedestrian signal heads are visible to provide clear crossing intervals for walkers.
hazards.location_in_image: At the intersection corners where traffic lights are mounted.

hazards.name: Sight line obstruction
hazards.description: Parked vehicles on the right side of the street near the intersection may block the view between drivers and pedestrians.
hazards.location_in_image: Right side of the roadway, adjacent to the crosswalk.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install dedicated pedestrian signal heads with countdown timers to improve clarity and safety for crossing pedestrians.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions (Bulb-outs)
interventions.description: Extend the sidewalk into the parking lane to shorten the crossing distance and increase pedestrian visibility.

interventions.title: Daylighting
interventions.description: Restrict parking immediately adjacent to the crosswalk to ensure clear sight lines for all road users.

result.summary: The image depicts a wide two-lane roadway with a high-visibility continental crosswalk and a sidewalk on the left side. While basic pedestrian infrastructure like curb ramps is present, the environment lacks traffic calming, signals, or a refuge island, resulting in a long unprotected crossing distance.

hazards.name: Uncontrolled Crossing
hazards.description: The marked crosswalk lacks any signage, signals, or flashing beacons to alert drivers to pedestrians.

hazards.name: Wide Roadway Geometry
hazards.description: The wide, open roadway design may encourage higher vehicle speeds and increases the time pedestrians are exposed to traffic.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs at the crossing to reduce the crossing distance and improve visibility between pedestrians and drivers.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Refuge Island
interventions.description: Add a raised median island to allow pedestrians to cross one direction of traffic at a time.

interventions.title: Rectangular Rapid Flashing Beacons (RRFB)
interventions.description: Install user-actuated flashing beacons to increase driver yield rates at this uncontrolled crossing.

result.summary: The pedestrian environment features a wide roadway with embedded transit tracks and a marked zebra crosswalk. While sidewalks and curb ramps are present, the lack of visible pedestrian signals and the wide crossing distance increase exposure risk.

hazards.name: Embedded transit tracks
hazards.description: Rail tracks in the roadway can cause tripping for pedestrians or catch bicycle tires, especially when wet.
hazards.location_in_image: Center of the roadway extending through the intersection

hazards.name: Wide crossing exposure
hazards.description: The width of the intersection increases the time pedestrians are exposed to potential vehicle traffic without a refuge.

interventions.title: Curb Extensions
interventions.description: Install bulb-outs to shorten the crossing distance and improve visibility between drivers and pedestrians.

interventions.title: Pedestrian Countdown Signals
interventions.description: Install signals to provide clear information on when it is safe to cross relative to transit and vehicle movements.

interventions.title: High-Visibility Crosswalk Refresh
interventions.description: Apply more durable, high-visibility thermoplastic markings to the existing crosswalk.
